sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
The path was a steady climb rather than a step change, with the only slow year FY2023 at 6.9% growth [D311].
FY2023's slowdown came as Intelligent Cloud and Productivity and Business Processes grew while More Personal Computing declined on Windows and Devices [P39][D932].
FY2026 reaccelerated to 17.8% growth, driven by Microsoft Cloud, with Intelligent Cloud led by Azure and Productivity and Business Processes by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud [D472][P17].
Microsoft Cloud reached 64.6% of revenue in FY2026 and contributed 16.2pp of the year's growth [D566][D568].
Server products and cloud services revenue rose 31% on Azure and other cloud services, which grew 41% on demand across workloads [P12][D641].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services added 5.1pp of growth, with cloud revenue up 17% on Copilot and E5 [D649][P14].
Operating income grew 20.8% against revenue growth of 17.8%, an incremental margin of 53.3% [D473][D472][D498].
Diluted EPS grew 31.6% against net income growth of 31.3%, with the diluted share count down 0.2% [D476][D474][D493].
Operating margin reached 46.8% in FY2026, a window high against a 41.7% median and 30.1% low [F50][D974][D975][D973].
Gross margin slipped 0.9pp to 67.9%, below its 68.2% median, as cost of revenue rose 21.1% against 17.8% revenue growth [F30][D486][D981][D489][D472].
Intelligent Cloud gross margin percentage fell on continued AI infrastructure investment and mix shift to Azure, partly offset by Azure efficiency gains [P11].
R&D fell to 10.7% of revenue, a window low, and selling and marketing to 8.0%, lifting operating margin 1.2pp [D450][D985][D451][D487].
Net margin rose 4.2pp to 40.3%, helped by $6.5 billion of net OpenAI investment gains in other income [D488][F70][P7].
Operating cash flow reached $182.9 billion in FY2026, 55.1% of revenue [F100][D457].
That increase was primarily due to higher cash received from customers and lower cash paid for income taxes [P1].
Free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion, a 20.2% margin and window low, as capex rose 79.6% to $115.9 billion [F120][D478][D456][D982][F110][D479].
Free cash flow was 0.50x net income against a 0.91x median, and capex ran 3.38x D&A [D460][D990][D461].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, 22.0% of revenue, in the 83rd percentile of six software peers against a -7.2% median [D465][D466][D1006][D1007].
Total debt fell 6.6% to $40.3 billion while cash and investments rose 2.9% to $113.2 billion [D464][D495][D463][D494].
Buybacks and dividends of $48.7 billion were 72.7% of free cash flow [D467][D468].
Return on average equity was 34.0%, below the 38.8% peer median, as equity grew 28.8% [D471][D1011][D482].
Free cash flow has run below 80% of net income for two years, at 0.70x in FY2025 and 0.50x in FY2026, the window low [R1][D406][D460][D988].
The gap reflects the capex build, with additions to property and equipment up $51.4 billion in FY2026 [P1][D479].
This is a deliberate AI infrastructure bet rather than an earnings-quality problem, but it leaves free cash flow margin at 20.2% against a 34.7% peer median [D456][D1003].
The FY2017 liquidity break means cash and investments and net cash omit short-term investments that year, so cross-gap comparisons are unreliable [R6][X158].
Free cash flow margin: a recovery above the 30.3% window median would confirm capex is peaking, while a print below the 20.2% FY2026 low would extend the squeeze [D984][D982].
Operating margin: holding above the 41.7% median would confirm the cost discipline, while a drop below it would reverse the FY2026 high of 46.8% [D975][D974].
Intelligent Cloud margin: a move back above the 42.0% FY2025 level would signal AI infrastructure costs are absorbing, while a further fall from 41.3% would extend the decline [D962][D963].
